description: REQ-109's new `defaulted_ms` field (added this revision to feed REQ-114's `computeRecentDefaultLossUsd`) is defined only in prose (behavioral-spec.md:2031-2036: 'This "defaulted" row ALSO carries a NEW `defaulted_ms` field ... the wall-clock time (`Date.now()`) at the moment THIS row itself is appended ... A row whose `status` is NOT "defaulted" ... carries no `defaulted_ms` field') — but REQ-109's OWN Acceptance Criteria section (behavioral-spec.md:2134-2152) contains ZERO test or structural check binding the REAL, production default-detection-and-append code to actually set this field when it appends a `"defaulted"` row, and none omitting it on non-defaulted rows. A full grep of both spec files for `defaulted_ms` (9 occurrences in behavioral-spec.md, 3 in verification-architecture.md) confirms every single one of them is EITHER (a) the original prose definition (REQ-109/REQ-114), OR (b) a test of `computeRecentDefaultLossUsd`/`computeOverallDefaultRateUsd`'s OWN pure-function correctness GIVEN a hand-authored fixture where `defaulted_ms` is ALREADY present and correctly populated as literal fixture data (PROP-114e/PROP-114f, verification-architecture.md:136-137) — never a check on the REAL REQ-109 append call site itself. This is precisely the class of gap this SAME document already identified and closed twice elsewhere in this SAME revision cycle for the kill-switch call sites: PROP-105h/PROP-114c explicitly exist because 'a mocked-caller fixture proving the function's own correctness is insufficient by itself' to prove 'the REAL, production REQ-106 issuance code actually calls this function' (behavioral-spec.md:806-809, resolving FIND-303/FIND-502) — but no analogous 'real production REQ-109 append code, not a hand-authored fixture, is confirmed to actually SET `defaulted_ms` at append time' proof obligation exists anywhere in the 171-row Proof Obligations table. Consequence: an implementation could pass EVERY stated PROP for REQ-109 (PROP-109a/b/c/e/f) and EVERY stated PROP for REQ-114 (PROP-114a/b/e/f) while the real, production `"defaulted"`-row-append code never actually sets `defaulted_ms` (e.g. a simple omission, a typo like `defaultedMs`, or a forgotten field in the append payload) — every REAL `"defaulted"` row in the live ledger would then have `defaulted_ms === undefined`. Per REQ-114's own fail-closed convention ('Malformed/negative/non-finite ... `defaulted_ms` on any row contributes `0` to the sum for that specific row', behavioral-spec.md:874-876), `computeRecentDefaultLossUsd` would silently treat every REAL default as outside its own window, and `totalRecentDefaultLossUsd` would be permanently `0` in production — the ENTIRE new absolute-loss defense this SAME revision adds to resolve FIND-602 would be silently, permanently inert, with every stated PROP still green, since none of them ever exercises the real append code path this field actually depends on.

evidence.snippet: This "defaulted" row ALSO carries a NEW `defaulted_ms` field ... A row whose `status` is NOT "defaulted" ... carries no `defaulted_ms` field. [REQ-109 Acceptance Criteria, lines 2134-2152, contains detectDefaultedLoans/adjustBalancesForOutstandingDebt/append-only/per-loan-lock checks only -- no defaulted_ms population check anywhere]

crossCheck.note: PROP-114e/PROP-114f (lines 136-137) each test computeRecentDefaultLossUsd against fixtures where defaulted_ms is supplied directly as literal fixture data -- neither is, or claims to be, a real-source-read confirming the production REQ-109 append call site sets this field. The REQ-109 PROP rows (PROP-109a/b/c/e/f, lines 161-166) list detectDefaultedLoans/adjustBalancesForOutstandingDebt/non-mutation/per-loan-lock/proportionality checks only. No PROP anywhere in the table mirrors PROP-105h's/PROP-114c's own 'the REAL, PRODUCTION ... code -- not a unit test in isolation ... genuinely ... sets/calls X' discipline for the defaulted_ms field specifically, even though this field is exactly as load-bearing for REQ-114's new absolute-loss signal as the kill-switch call sites are for REQ-106's issuance flow.
